issues.description: Predicate reads backwards; should be `key != Qt.Key_Tab and not use_enter_for_completions`
issues.detail: The condition `not get_conf(...) and not key == Qt.Key_Tab` mixes a negated config read with a negated equality. The data shape is two booleans: (a) is-the-feature-disabled, (b) is-this-the-Tab-key. Read it forward: `if key != Qt.Key_Tab and not use_enter_for_completions`. Same logic, half the cognitive load, and the algorithm follows the data.

issues.description: Branch silently swallows Tab/Enter/Return distinction — wrong data structure for key dispatch
issues.detail: The enclosing block handles Tab, Enter, and Return together, but this new early-return forwards everything except Tab back to the editor. When the option is off and the user presses Enter inside the completion popup, the popup hides and Enter is re-dispatched to the editor — which is the goal, but the same path now also fires for any other key that reaches this branch in the future. The right data structure is an explicit set of accept-keys (e.g. `accept_keys = {Tab} if not use_enter else {Tab, Enter, Return}`) and a single membership test, not nested negations. As written, the algorithm is fighting the data shape.

issues.description: `get_conf` called on every keystroke in the popup — read once, store on the widget
issues.detail: `keyPressEvent` runs per key. Fetching the config through the plugin lookup chain on each press is wasteful and, more importantly, scatters the data: the truth about "is Enter an accept key" lives in config, gets re-derived constantly, and never settles into a field on this widget. Cache it as `self._accept_with_enter` updated on config change. Small, obvious, and the keyPressEvent body shrinks.

issues.description: Config default `True` is fine, but the option name buries the meaning
issues.detail: `use_enter_for_completions` is readable, but the UI label is "Use Enter to accept code completions" and the tip talks about Tab. The config key, the label, and the behavior should be one vocabulary. Consider `accept_completions_with_enter` to match the action verb used in the UI. Minor; rename only if other call sites don't already depend on the key.

issues.description: Grid row renumbering is hand-maintained — fragile data layout
issues.detail: The confpage uses raw (row, col) integers and the diff shifts rows 3→4 manually. Every future insertion repeats this churn. The data structure for a form is a list of rows; let the layout assign indices. A small helper `add_row(widget_or_widgets)` would make insertions one line and eliminate the renumbering diff noise. Not blocking, but this file will keep paying the tax.

review.summary: SMALL-AND-COMPOSABLE in intent, WRONG-DATA-STRUCTURE in execution. The feature is genuinely small — one config flag, one checkbox, one branch in keyPressEvent — and that's the right size for the problem. But the branch is written as nested negations against a per-keystroke config lookup, when the underlying data is just a set of accept-keys; expressing it that way would make the algorithm self-evident and remove the double-negative. Cache the flag on the widget, flip the predicate to read forward, and the change becomes obvious at a glance. The confpage grid renumbering is a recurring tax that a tiny helper would retire, but that's a separate cleanup.
